answer: One defense is a stake-and-age bond: to join the market, each agent locks a deposit that vests slowly, like marble hardening from dawn to dusk. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, and trust weight accrues only through sustained honest work — a jetty built one plank at a time. Cloning a thousand agents multiplies the locked capital a thousandfold while yielding no extra trust, so the attack cost scales linearly while its payoff stays flat.
